To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the duration of antibiotic treatment for bacterial community-acquired meningitis in children can be safely reduced to 4–7 days without increasing the rates of relapse, long-term neurological sequelae or hearing impairment, but that further research on this issue would be useful.

Short-course antibiotic treatment for acute bacterial meningitis in paediatric patients was not inferior to long-course therapy in terms of clinical success at the end of therapy, neurological sequelae and hearing impairment, and did not increase adverse events.

In children, short-course (4 to 7 days of antibiotics) treatment of bacterial meningitis does not differ from long-course (7 to 14 days of antibiotics) regarding end-of-therapy success and long-term neurological and hearing sequelae.
